requirements.title: Project Branding and Product Name
requirements.definition: The product must present the client-approved Harbor Quill identity, including any later approved transition to ArchiveLedger.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the displayed product identity only; page-specific marketing copy and layout are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Portugal Landing-Page Geoblock
requirements.definition: Access to the Harbor Quill landing page must follow the client-directed Portugal geoblocking policy.
requirements.boundary_note: Geographic access control can be changed independently of payment-provider availability or business jurisdiction.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Content and Layout
requirements.definition: The landing page must render the approved hero, mechanics messaging, calls to action, terminology, and responsive layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers general page copy and layout; book-cover rendering, FAQs, badges, and live platform figures have separate failure trajectories.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Book-Cover Presentation
requirements.definition: The landing page must show the book cover at an appropriate compact size with every edge visible and without cropping.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from the broader landing-page layout because cover size and cropping repeatedly failed and changed independently.

requirements.title: Product FAQ Content
requirements.definition: The site must publish the approved FAQ explanations of purchasing, referrals, commissions, tickets, prizes, wallets, fees, access, and support.
requirements.boundary_note: This is rendered product copy; the underlying behaviors described by the FAQ remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Milestone Partner Rewards
requirements.definition: The historical milestone-partner reward mechanism is an independently removable gamification behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: Retained as a historical Requirement because its first visible evidence removes the whole mechanism; no hidden introduction is assumed.

requirements.title: Small Block Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The system must fund, trigger, and award the independently evolving Small Block prize according to its configured pool, sales trigger, winner count, and prize amount.
requirements.boundary_note: Winner count, award amount, trigger, and pool funding are attributes of one draw mechanism; ticket issuance and claim interaction are separately testable.

requirements.title: Big Block Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The system historically maintained an independently configurable Big Block prize mechanism with its own trigger, winner count, award amount, and pool.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept separate from Small Block because its parameters changed independently and the entire mechanism was later removed.

requirements.title: Prize-Ticket Lifecycle
requirements.definition: Prize tickets must be associated with the applicable active draw and expire, burn, reset, or carry forward according to the approved block lifecycle.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers what happens to issued tickets over draw boundaries; issuance for coded and no-code purchases is represented separately.

requirements.title: Chainlink VRF Winner Selection
requirements.definition: Random prize and weighted-recipient selection must use configured Chainlink VRF randomness and be verifiable on-chain.
requirements.boundary_note: Randomness infrastructure can fail or be reconfigured independently of prize amounts and payout interaction.

requirements.title: Prize Claim Flow
requirements.definition: Prize winners must be able to redeem an award through the approved claim control, with visibility limited to the applicable eligibility window.
requirements.boundary_note: Claim interaction is independently testable from winner selection and from automatic referral-commission payout.

requirements.title: Aave Prize-Pool Yield Connector
requirements.definition: Prize-pool funds may be deposited through an Aave connector to generate yield when that integration is active.
requirements.boundary_note: An independent integration that can be removed without removing the underlying prize pools.

requirements.title: Coded-Referral Commission
requirements.definition: When a valid referral code is used, the associated existing NFT or account must receive the configured commission automatically.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from ticket issuance because commissions and tickets repeatedly had different accounting failures and amounts.

requirements.title: Coded-Referral Ticket Issuance
requirements.definition: When a valid referral code is used, the associated existing NFT must receive the configured prize-ticket entries.
requirements.boundary_note: Ticket quantities are attributes of this issuance behavior; commission transfer is a separate independently failing mechanism.

requirements.title: No-Referral Commission Allocation
requirements.definition: When a mint omits a referral code, its commission must be assigned to an eligible existing NFT through the approved weighted or rotation-based random process.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from no-referral ticket allocation because one reward could register while the other remained missing.

requirements.title: No-Referral Ticket Allocation
requirements.definition: When a mint omits a referral code, the configured ticket entries must be created and assigned to an eligible existing NFT through the approved random process.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept independent from commission allocation due to distinct issuance, reconciliation, and display failures.

requirements.title: Referral-Code Validation
requirements.definition: Checkout must accept only referral identifiers belonging to NFTs finalized before the purchase and must prevent self-referrals or future-token identifiers.
requirements.boundary_note: Validation can fail independently of later commission and ticket distribution.

requirements.title: NFT Referral Identity
requirements.definition: Each NFT must use its own assigned mint or token serial as its permanent referral code and expose that value consistently.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers identity assignment and display, not validation of a code entered during another buyer's checkout.

requirements.title: Unlimited-Mint NFT Ebook
requirements.definition: The ebook must be sold as an open or unlimited-mint NFT edition rather than a capped collection.
requirements.boundary_note: Supply policy is independent of accepted payment assets, pricing, and referral allocation.

requirements.title: Mint Price and Revenue Split
requirements.definition: Each mint must charge the configured price and divide proceeds among the founder, affiliate commission, and active prize pool according to the approved allocation.
requirements.boundary_note: The price and allocation shares are attributes of one settlement mechanism; payment-asset-specific execution is separate.

requirements.title: USDC Wallet Mint Flow
requirements.definition: A connected wallet must be able to approve USDC and complete exactly one NFT mint, with success recorded only after the mint transaction confirms.
requirements.boundary_note: USDC approval-to-mint execution had a distinct failure trajectory from ETH swaps and from generic success-modal rendering.

requirements.title: ETH Wallet Mint Flow
requirements.definition: A connected wallet must be able to pay with ETH through the configured swap path and receive the NFT when the on-chain mint completes.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers successful ETH payment and mint execution; excess-input refund denomination and calculation are separately configurable.

requirements.title: ETH Pricing and Excess Refund
requirements.definition: ETH checkout must calculate sufficient input for the fixed mint price, consume only the required amount, reject shortfalls, and return excess value in the approved asset.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from basic ETH minting because the mint could execute while refund UX or denomination remained unacceptable.

requirements.title: Payment Method Selection and Disclosure
requirements.definition: Checkout must clearly display the supported settlement currency and allow customers to choose when multiple enabled payment methods are available.
requirements.boundary_note: This UI behavior can be wrong even when individual USDC, ETH, or card payment implementations are correct.

requirements.title: Transak Fiat Minting
requirements.definition: Non-crypto buyers must be able to use Transak-supported fiat methods to acquire the payment asset, receive a non-custodial wallet, and mint the NFT.
requirements.boundary_note: Provider choice, hidden wallet creation, and fiat-to-USDC mint completion are one integrated fiat path; its lifecycle may be deferred without affecting crypto minting.

requirements.title: Optional Mint Gratuity
requirements.definition: Checkout must offer an optional gratuity with approved presets and a custom amount, process it separately when required, and avoid self-tipping.
requirements.boundary_note: Tip settlement and its delayed follow-up explanation are one optional payment mechanism, independent of the NFT purchase itself.

requirements.title: Mint Result Feedback
requirements.definition: Success feedback must appear only after a confirmed mint, show the correct token identifier, and present scenario-appropriate referral and reward status.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from payment execution because false success messages occurred without a mint and could recur from stale UI state.

requirements.title: Base Network Deployment
requirements.definition: The NFT contracts and production blockchain interactions must operate on the approved Base network environment.
requirements.boundary_note: Network choice is independent of NFT standard, payment asset, and application hosting.

requirements.title: Secondary Royalty Enforcement
requirements.definition: Secondary-market transfers must enforce the approved flat royalty using an NFT standard and marketplace controls capable of supporting that policy.
requirements.boundary_note: ERC-721C and marketplace whitelisting are implementation attributes of the independently required royalty mechanism.

requirements.title: NFT Transfer Semantics
requirements.definition: When an NFT is transferred or sold, the approved book access, referral identity, badges, and applicable active ticket state must follow the asset.
requirements.boundary_note: This defines state ownership across transfers, not royalty collection or the one-off transfer of a specified test NFT.

requirements.title: NFT Metadata Accuracy
requirements.definition: NFT metadata and detail attributes must expose accurate live referral, ticket, commission, earnings, badge, and referral-code values from the authoritative state.
requirements.boundary_note: Metadata for an individual NFT is separate from aggregate dashboard and leaderboard statistics.

requirements.title: NFT Asset Rendering and Discovery
requirements.definition: Minted NFTs must appear for their owner in supported wallet and dashboard views with working image, metadata, and detail-page resources.
requirements.boundary_note: Asset discovery and media rendering can fail while ownership is valid and while the separately gated ebook reader remains unavailable.

requirements.title: NFT Badge Awards
requirements.definition: NFTs must receive only the approved badges when their referral or achievement thresholds are actually satisfied.
requirements.boundary_note: Award eligibility and state accuracy are separate from icon choice, badge count, and responsive layout.

requirements.title: Badge Set and Presentation
requirements.definition: The interface must present the approved curated badge set, names, icons, ordering, and responsive row layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Visual curation and responsive arrangement can change independently of whether a badge was correctly earned.

requirements.title: Wallet Authentication
requirements.definition: Crypto users must be able to authenticate through a connected wallet using SIWE for protected wallet-based flows.
requirements.boundary_note: Wallet authentication can evolve independently of email magic links and public unauthenticated APIs.

requirements.title: Email Magic-Link Authentication
requirements.definition: Users, including fiat buyers without an established wallet workflow, must be able to access their dashboard through low-friction email authentication.
requirements.boundary_note: Authentication-token delivery is related to but distinct from general transactional-email notifications.

requirements.title: Unauthenticated Public APIs
requirements.definition: Public information such as leaderboards and prize-pool values must remain accessible without user authentication.
requirements.boundary_note: Public read access is independent of wallet and email authentication used for protected account functions.

requirements.title: Transactional Email Delivery
requirements.definition: The configured email service must reliably deliver verification, mint confirmation, reward, badge, and winner notifications with accurate content.
requirements.boundary_note: Provider configuration and message delivery form one email subsystem; email-based login semantics remain separate.

requirements.title: Removable IPFS Ebook Storage
requirements.definition: The ebook PDF must be stored through Pinata on IPFS in a way that preserves the client's ability to remove or replace the hosted content.
requirements.boundary_note: Storage location and removability are independent of ownership gating and reader navigation.

requirements.title: NFT-Holder-Gated Book Access
requirements.definition: Only a wallet holding a valid active NFT may decrypt and open the ebook through the Lit Protocol ownership check.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers authorization and decryption; page navigation and mobile-wallet interoperability have separate trajectories.

requirements.title: Ebook Reader Navigation
requirements.definition: The PDF.js-based reader must display the ebook and provide usable page navigation through visible or recoverable controls and keyboard input.
requirements.boundary_note: Reader interaction can fail after successful authorization and decryption, so it is separate from access control.

requirements.title: Mobile Wallet Book Access
requirements.definition: NFT holders using supported mobile wallet applications and embedded browsers must be able to complete the ownership signature and open the ebook.
requirements.boundary_note: Mobile embedded-wallet interoperability showed failures distinct from desktop access and reader navigation.

requirements.title: Dashboard and Leaderboard Accuracy
requirements.definition: Dashboard, leaderboard, home-page, and NFT-summary figures must consistently reflect actual mints, ownership, referrals, tickets, commissions, earnings, badges, supply, and prize-pool state.
requirements.boundary_note: Aggregate and account-level reporting is separate from the underlying reward transfer and from per-NFT metadata generation.

requirements.title: Production Contract-Event Webhook
requirements.definition: The backend must receive and route production Base contract events through the configured Alchemy webhook and contract-address filter.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently configured operational behavior required for reward finalization and data synchronization.

requirements.title: Contract Migration Data Continuity
requirements.definition: Replacement-contract deployment must preserve or deliberately reconcile approved existing user, NFT, reward, and backend data without silently mixing obsolete contract state.
requirements.boundary_note: A migration-specific acceptance condition, distinct from normal dashboard accuracy and contract-event ingestion.

requirements.title: Help and Contact Form
requirements.definition: The landing page must provide a help or contact entry point with the approved inquiry fields and submission control.
requirements.boundary_note: A product support interface independent of the external Discord community.

requirements.title: Discord Community Server
requirements.definition: The project must provide an operational Discord community with approved onboarding, information, discussion, support, product, moderation, and voice channels.
requirements.boundary_note: The community server is an independently requested operational deliverable, not generic project communication.

requirements.title: Malicious-Site Warning Remediation
requirements.definition: The production domain must be submitted through the applicable false-positive and developer-verification channels to remove erroneous wallet or browser phishing warnings.
requirements.boundary_note: A concrete production-access remediation task, not a general security or QA Requirement.

requirements.title: Specified NFT Ownership Transfer
requirements.definition: The requested mint or affiliate identifier must be transferred to the client-designated wallet.
requirements.boundary_note: A one-off on-chain data mutation distinct from the general rules governing secondary transfers.
